title: Strict early teachers
summary: Howard says his teachers were strong and struck him when he got things wrong; he studied clarinet and cornet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: So let's start out with your early childhood and when you began to get into music and some of your teachers and some of your activities. How about that.
Okay, sir, if you're going to call me Mister, I'll act like a Mister. You know, Buddy, if you knew how I was taught to play music, if you knew how I was
taught to play music, you would be surprised.
Can you tell us how you were taught and what your teachers were like?
Well, the teachers were very -- mostly, they were ordinary people, but they were strong people and they had a mind to get you to play. In other words, they'd knock me out.
What do you mean, knock you out?
They were very strict. They didn't take no foolishness with me. I didn't get the thing right, they'd say you know that's not right, Paul, why don't you do it right, boom. Just like that.
I was studying clarinet, studying what is another -- oh, a cornet. A clarinet, a cornet, and one other instrument I was playing. I can't think of it, but it will come to me after while.
Were you playing a saxophone at that point?
A wind instrument, wasn't a French horn?
No, it wasn't the French horn. But
